findings.problem: 'Hunger in one place pushes them to start over in another' gives a reason for the move. Ruth 1:1 mentions the famine and says they went, but it doesn't say the famine is why.
'Egypt is a place God's people went during other hard times' is a Bible fact with no reference.
'Keeping those details sharp helps you track where God is working' is preachy and flat, with no humor.
'Edom was a neighbor country' has no reference. 'The writer wants us to notice Moab in particular' adds an intent the text doesn't state.
Generic and flat. 'At the very center of what God is doing in this book' is a preachy claim and not a Bible fact from this passage.
'A well-known woman in Genesis' is a Bible fact with no reference.
'Those are the names to keep in your hands here' is an awkward phrase and doesn't sound like Papa Dorin. There is no humor.
'Dinah appears in Genesis' has no reference. 'The writer is pointing us to Ruth's name on purpose' adds an intent the text doesn't state. 'Key to... God's plan' goes beyond the passage.
Somber and generic, with no personality. The line about the weight she is carrying reads like a sermon.

'The famine that once pushed her out is easing' and 'That mercy... is what turns her feet back toward Bethlehem' add reasons the text doesn't give. Ruth 1:6 only says she heard this and prepared to leave.
'A king will come into Israel's story later' has no reference. 'The LORD has visited His people' changes the BSB wording ('attended to'). 'That provision is what pulls Naomi homeward' adds a reason.
'Bread on the table is the victory' brings in a food other than cookies, and it isn't the Scripture food being covered. This breaks the Food rule.
'She loves them enough to release them' is Naomi's motive stated as fact. It isn't marked as his own guess ('I think') and the text doesn't say it.
'She is trying to free them from the hard road she is on' adds a reason the text doesn't give.
'Her new husband' is wrong, since the verse says 'your new husband' (each daughter-in-law's). 'She wants them to have stability and care again' adds a reason the text doesn't give.
'Her new husband' misstates the verse. 'That is her picture of a settled, safe future for them' is an interpretation stated as fact.
'Their hearts are set on staying with her' states a feeling as fact, and it isn't marked as his own guess.
'She is showing how unrealistic that path would be' and 'trying to talk them out of tying their future to her emptiness' add reasons the text doesn't give.
'Her point is that they need real, near-term hope' adds a reason the text doesn't give. 'Stay from having husbands' garbles 'refrain from having husbands'.
'She is showing them how empty her own prospects are' adds a reason the text doesn't give. 'Stay from having husbands' garbles the verse.
'That is how her losses feel from the inside' and 'deep hurt and confusion' state her feelings as fact, not marked as his own guess.
'What God has allowed' adds to the text. Naomi says the hand of the LORD 'has gone out against' her, and says nothing about allowing.
Flat and generic, with no humor or Papa Dorin voice.
'It shows she loved Naomi' adds a reason or feeling the text doesn't state. It isn't marked as his own guess.
'Her first loud action of loyalty' adds 'first' and 'loud', which the text doesn't say.
'Naomi is still trying to release Ruth from a hard future' and 'She is not expecting the answer she is about to hear' add motives and expectations the text doesn't give.
'Naomi keeps pushing Ruth toward an easier path' adds a reason the text doesn't give.
'A covenant kind of statement' and 'about belonging and worship more than customs' add interpretation the text doesn't state.
Flat and generic, with no humor or Papa Dorin voice where a warm line would fit.
Flat and generic, with no personality.
'Time and sorrow have changed her' and 'recognition and surprise' add things the text doesn't say. They aren't marked as his own guess.
'Her very appearance tells a story' adds something the text doesn't say.
'They recognize her, even through all the change' adds something the text doesn't say. The text shows only the question.
'Hannah is another woman of faith in Scripture' has no reference.
'Leah is a different woman in Genesis' has no reference.
'The story will show us more of what God is doing behind that feeling' is preachy and generic.
'God is already lining up provision in the background' and 'harvest time will open doors for them' add claims the text doesn't state.
'God will start answering needs Naomi can barely put into words yet' adds a claim the text doesn't state.
'It sets up how Ruth will find work and favor' states what the harvest timing is for. Ruth 1:22 doesn't say that.
